call.review_scope: Prepared remarks and selected Q&A read; complete original audio not independently listened to
call.paraphrase: Management said the Google revenue expected through FY2028 was already in its previous custom-silicon outlook, with larger incremental opportunity later. It attributed lower near-term gross margins to custom-product mix, discussed 57.5%–58.5% non-GAAP gross margin, preliminary 13% FY2028 non-GAAP tax, and roughly 2,550 FY2027 non-GAAP operating expense. Capacity prepayments of about 1,000 during FY2027 were expected to support supplier availability and later be applied against material purchases. These are prospective management statements, not paid-cash facts. In Q&A, leadership described a multi-year transition from copper toward optical connectivity with overlapping technologies. That supports an adoption ramp and capacity-investment requirement, not immediate monetization of the entire addressable market.
call.use: Only short paraphrase redistributed; primary filings/releases/deck take precedence for reported financial facts. No full transcript in the public package.

interview.event: Matt Murphy on CNBC Mad Money, interview with Jim Cramer
interview.source_type: Publisher interview hosted on official Marvell video site; player-provided English captions reviewed
interview.review_scope: Full 612.8-second caption file read; captions not independently audio-verified
interview.paraphrase: Murphy described the revised FY2027/FY2028 revenue outlook (01:23–01:43), which the later October investor day superseded for FY2028. His earlier-target comparison (02:26–03:35) mixes realized history with still-forecast FY2027/FY2028 figures, so it is not a clean actual-versus-prior-guidance scorecard. He linked connectivity growth to earlier compute/memory investment (04:14–04:41), described the Google warrant as an exchange tied to large cumulative revenue milestones (06:05–06:29), and emphasized engineering execution and supply-chain trust (06:49–07:36). Claims of custom relationships with all four major hyperscalers and optics leadership (07:53–08:47) remain management assertions, not independent market-share measurements. His aspirational valuation discussion is not an input to this DCF.
interview.rights: Public-safe paraphrase only. Full third-party caption source retained privately outside the public package.
